canonical_statement: The study re-evaluated memory-based self-improving web agents to test reliability under repeated runs and altered task order, then examined underspecification as a possible source of fragility.
The evaluation compared Agent Workflow Memory and ReasoningBank on WebArena, VisualWebArena, and SCUBA using updated baseline agent harnesses.
WebArena contributed 812 web-browsing tasks across Shopping, Shopping Admin, GitLab, Reddit, Map, and Multisite domains.
VisualWebArena contributed 910 tasks across Classifieds, Reddit, and Shopping domains.
After excluding tasks invalidated by website updates, SCUBA contributed 267 enterprise web tasks.

population.label: SCUBA tasks retained after invalid-task exclusions

canonical_statement: For experiments of interest, the authors ran three identical repetitions, reported average pass@1, cross-run standard deviation, and best-worst run gap, and tested the default order plus two shuffled task orders.

GPT-5-mini was used as both the agent backbone and memory-construction model unless otherwise specified, and ground-truth task reward was supplied during memory construction to avoid confounding from a noisy LLM judge.
Memory-based self-improvement increased cross-run pass@1 variance in 17 of 24 benchmark-domain/method cases (about 71%).

canonical_statement: Among the 24 variance comparisons, 11 showed a relative increase in standard deviation greater than 50% after adding memory-based self-improvement.

canonical_statement: On the WebArena GitLab subset, the best-worst pass@1 gap across three runs was 4.44 percentage points for the baseline and 7.78 points with ReasoningBank.

canonical_statement: Across all WebArena tasks, average pass@1 over three runs was 54.8% for the baseline, 54.1% with AWM, and 56.3% with ReasoningBank.
ReasoningBank improved WebArena average pass@1 by 1.5 percentage points over the stronger baseline, but this three-run comparison had p=0.23.

canonical_statement: The default benchmark task ordering was not difficulty-neutral: WebArena domains showed an implicit easy-to-hard curriculum, while VisualWebArena Shopping showed a more complex nonuniform difficulty pattern.
When the task sequence was shuffled, performance degraded significantly in 6 of 8 tested memory-method/order cases shown for WebArena and VisualWebArena.

canonical_statement: Environment underspecification caused the memory constructor to save plausible but infeasible strategies, including API-based actions that were unsupported in the browser-only environment.

canonical_statement: Ambiguous task wording could cause the agent to misinterpret benchmark intent, overthink failures, and write memories that were irrelevant to the actual executable task.

source_anchor.paragraph: 4.1 Uncovering the Failure Modes in Memory Construction

canonical_statement: Evaluator false negatives could seed spurious memories: an answer of $0.00 was treated as failing a strict string-match requirement for 0, after which the agent generated an irrelevant corrective memory.

An unintended Haversine-distance fallback could enter memory after receiving reward and then be retrieved more often on later map tasks, illustrating stochastic propagation of a questionable strategy.

To reduce underspecification during ReasoningBank memory construction, the authors tested rubric-and-score feedback, environment action feedback, a prompt that stated supported and unsupported strategies, and the combination of all three.
Under Shuffle-1, combining rubric information, environment feedback, and prompt modification increased ReasoningBank pass rate from 49.8% to 52.7%, a 2.9-point gain.

concept.text: ReasoningBank + rubric + environment feedback + prompt modification

canonical_statement: Under Shuffle-2, the combined underspecification mitigation increased ReasoningBank pass rate from 50.7% to 51.8%, a 1.1-point gain.

canonical_statement: The authors report that the combined specification interventions recovered 31% of the observed degradation, leaving 69% of the performance gap unresolved.

concept.text: Fraction of task-order performance degradation recovered

canonical_statement: The authors recommend reporting self-improving-agent results across multiple runs and randomized task orders rather than relying on a single run.
The authors recommend first piloting self-improving methods on well-specified tasks and then stress-testing them on underspecified tasks to estimate worst-case behavior before deployment.
The authors argue that stored agent memories should be treated as unverified hypotheses and that future systems need validation mechanisms that filter problematic memories before they can cascade.
The authors motivate human-oversight interfaces that let operators inspect and correct wrong lessons during iterative specification before failures propagate in a real deployment.

The evaluation was limited to two memory-based self-improvement methods in web-browsing environments and did not cover other self-improvement paradigms, other domains, or the newest memory-management methods.
The qualitative memory audit covered only a subset of generated memories, so additional failure modes may remain undocumented.
A no-memory run over all 812 WebArena tasks cost about $25 with GPT-5-mini, while a no-memory run over all 267 SCUBA tasks cost about $29; memory methods added extra model-call and context costs.
